title: Herder settings
description: Herder's user settings, at ~/.config/herder/settings.json or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herder/settings.json. Holds only what differs from the default; a missing key is the default. Secrets are never here: the Anthropic API key and the GitHub tokens are kept in the Keychain.

$schema.description: Where this schema is published. Ignored by Herder, and put back when it writes the file.

updates.description: Finding and installing new releases of Herder.

check_automatically.description: Check for a new release once a day without being asked. Herder asks before installing anything.

agents.description: The coding agents a session can be started with, beside the built-in ones.

first_prompt_template.description: Wraps the text typed in a New order before the agent sees it. {prompt} stands for the text. Without it, the template goes first, then a blank line, then the text. Empty sends the text as typed.

custom.description: Your own agents, in the order menus list them. Each is a command run in your login shell, in the root of the worktree a session starts in.

show_whitespace.description: Which whitespace gets a marker: a dot for a space, an arrow for a tab and a hook for a line ending. Only drawn on screen; never part of the text. trailing marks the spaces and tabs at the end of a line, and not line endings.

word_wrap.description: Break long lines at word boundaries instead of scrolling sideways. A word longer than the line breaks at a character.

wrap_column.description: How many characters of the code font fit on a line before it wraps. Without it, lines wrap at the window's edge. A line never gets wider than the window. Has no effect while word_wrap is off, and is kept for when it is turned on.

providers.description: The services Herder itself calls, as opposed to the agents it runs.

anthropic.description: Where calls to Claude go, such as the one that names a New order. The API key is kept in the Keychain, never here.

endpoint.description: An Anthropic-compatible base URL. The default is Meridian's local API, which needs no key.

id.description: What the agent used last, saved tabs and the session history call this agent. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; unique, and not a built-in agent's (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi). Changing it loses the agent's history.

type.description: A built-in agent this one is a variant of. Every field left out takes that agent's value, and environment is laid over its environment. An empty string clears a command the built-in agent has.

name.description: What menus call the agent. Without one, the type's name, or none.

command.description: The command line that starts a new session. {session} stands for the session's id. Without one, the type's command.

plan_command.description: The command line that starts a new session in Plan mode, used instead of command. Without one, Plan runs command.

prompt_argument.description: Added to the end of the command line to give a new session its first prompt. {prompt} stands for the prompt, quoted for the shell. Without one, the agent starts with no prompt.

prompt_needs_return.description: The agent only fills its input with the first prompt, so Herder sends Return once it shows.

resume_command.description: The command line that picks a session up again after its terminal was closed. {session} stands for the session's id. Without one, the session starts afresh.

session_lookup.description: For an agent that names its own sessions: a command line that lists them, which Herder reads to learn the id of the session a tab started.

environment.description: Variables set for the agent's terminal alone, over the app's own and, with a type, over that agent's.
